paragraphs.text_en: Around the world, more and more people are moving from the countryside to cities. This process, known as **urban** **migration**, is driven by the search for better **opportunities** — jobs, education, and **services** that are often easier to find in **urban** areas. Cities offer good **transport** links, hospitals, universities, and cultural attractions that many **rural** areas lack.
paragraphs.text_vi: Trên khắp thế giới, ngày càng nhiều người di chuyển từ nông thôn lên thành phố. Quá trình này, được gọi là **di cư đô thị**, được thúc đẩy bởi việc tìm kiếm các **cơ hội** tốt hơn — việc làm, giáo dục và **dịch vụ** thường dễ tiếp cận hơn ở các khu vực **đô thị**.

paragraphs.text_en: However, city life also has drawbacks. Large **populations** make cities **crowded** and expensive. Long **commutes** — journeys from home to work — can be tiring and stressful. Many people choose to live in the **suburbs** — quieter areas outside the city centre — to enjoy more space while still having **access** to city **services**.
paragraphs.text_vi: Tuy nhiên, cuộc sống đô thị cũng có những hạn chế. **Dân số** đông làm cho các thành phố trở nên **đông đúc** và đắt đỏ. Những chuyến **đi lại** dài có thể gây mệt mỏi. Nhiều người chọn sống ở **vùng ngoại ô** để có thêm không gian trong khi vẫn có **quyền tiếp cận** các **dịch vụ** thành phố.

paragraphs.text_en: In contrast, **rural** life offers a **peaceful** environment, clean air, and a strong sense of community. However, people in the countryside often face challenges such as limited **transport**, fewer job opportunities, and reduced **access** to healthcare and education. This creates a **gap** in quality of life between city and country dwellers.
paragraphs.text_vi: Ngược lại, cuộc sống **nông thôn** mang lại môi trường **yên bình**, không khí trong lành và tình cảm cộng đồng gắn bó. Tuy nhiên, người ở nông thôn thường phải đối mặt với những thách thức như **giao thông** hạn chế và **tiếp cận** ít hơn. Điều này tạo ra một **khoảng cách** về chất lượng cuộc sống.

paragraphs.text_en: **Poverty** can affect both city and **rural** populations, though it often looks different in each setting. Improving **transport** links and **services** in the countryside can give rural residents the same **lifestyle** choices as those in the city.
paragraphs.text_vi: **Đói nghèo** có thể ảnh hưởng đến cả **dân số** thành thị và nông thôn. Cải thiện các liên kết **giao thông** và **dịch vụ** ở nông thôn có thể mang lại cho người dân nông thôn những lựa chọn **lối sống** giống như người ở thành phố.

ex5_error_fix.instruction: Each sentence has one underlined word or phrase that is wrong. Choose the correct replacement.

items.sentence: She moved to [suburb] areas outside the city centre to find more space for her growing family.
items.explanation: 'Suburban' is the adjective needed before the plural noun 'areas'. 'Suburb' and 'suburbs' are nouns.
items.explanation_vi: 'Suburban' là adjective cần trước plural noun 'areas'. 'Suburb' và 'suburbs' là nouns.

items.sentence: The city's [populate] has grown by 20% in the last ten years.
People in rural areas often have [limit] access to good public transport.
items.explanation_vi: Cần adjective: tiếp cận hạn chế.

items.sentence: His daily commute to the city [take] over ninety minutes each way.
items.explanation: Third person singular: his commute takes.
items.explanation_vi: Third person singular: cuộc đi lại của anh ấy mất.

items.sentence: The gap between urban and rural lifestyles is [grow] every year.
items.explanation: Present continuous form needed: is growing.

ex6_sd.instruction: Do sentences A and B have the same meaning (S) or different meanings (D)?

items.b: The area is becoming more crowded.
items.explanation: A rapidly increasing population and a place becoming more crowded both describe the same situation — more people are living in the same space.
Rural and peaceful are often used together to describe the calm, quiet lifestyle of the countryside. In this context, the sentences carry the same meaning.

items.a: People migrate to the city for a better life.
items.b: People move to the city for a better life.
items.explanation: Migrate and move both describe the action of going from one place to live in another. These sentences express the same idea.

items.a: The gap between rich and poor is large.
items.b: The difference between rich and poor is large.
items.explanation: Gap and difference both describe an inequality between two things. In this context, these sentences carry the same meaning.

items.a: The city offers many opportunities for young people.
items.b: The city offers many chances for young people.
items.explanation: Opportunity and chance both mean a favourable situation that allows someone to do something. These sentences say the same thing.
Urban and rural are opposites. Urban describes a city environment; rural describes a countryside environment. These sentences describe completely different areas.
Crowded and peaceful are opposites in this context. Crowded means full of people and noise; peaceful means calm and quiet.

items.a: She migrates to the city permanently.
items.b: She commutes to the city every day.
items.explanation: Migrate means to move permanently to a new place. Commute means to travel regularly between home and work without moving permanently. These describe very different situations.

items.b: The area has good access to services.
items.explanation: Poverty describes a severe lack of money and resources. Having good access to services describes a well-connected area. These sentences describe opposite situations.

items.b: She lives in the urban centre.
items.explanation: A suburb is a residential area on the edge of a city. An urban centre is the city itself. These describe different locations relative to the city.

grammar_spotlight.vi_grammar_point: Cấu trúc so sánh hơn nâng cao
grammar_spotlight.source_ref: Murphy, R. (2019). English Grammar in Use (5th ed.). Cambridge University Press.

form.positive: Subject + Verb + more + Adjective + than + Object
form.negative: Subject + Verb + not as + Adjective + as + Object
form.question: Is/Are + Subject + more + Adjective + than + Object?
form.variant: Comparative with -er (e.g., bigger, faster) + than + Object

grammar_spotlight.rule_vi: Cấu trúc so sánh hơn dùng để so sánh mức độ của hai đối tượng. Khi tính từ ngắn (một âm tiết) hoặc có dạng -er, dùng dạng tính từ + er/thân + than; với tính từ dài (hai âm tiết trở lên) dùng more/less + adjective + than. Đối với so sánh bằng, dùng not as + adjective + as. Cấu trúc chung: more/less + adjective + than … hoặc not as + adjective + as ….
grammar_spotlight.rule_en: Use the comparative form to compare two things, with more/less/not as … as + adjective + than/as.
grammar_spotlight.common_error: ❌ City is more crowded then countryside.  →  ✅ City is more crowded than the countryside.
in_context: Cities are more crowded than rural areas.
Living in the suburbs offers more space than the city centre.
Rural life is not as expensive as city life.

usage_notes.text: Sau dạng so sánh hơn luôn cần từ 'than' để nối với đối tượng so sánh.
examples: ❌ He is taller his brother → ✅ He is taller than his brother

usage_notes.text: Cấu trúc 'not as … as' diễn tả mức độ thấp hơn hoặc bằng nhau; khi muốn nói mức độ cao hơn, dùng comparative.
examples: ✅ The car is not as fast as the bike. (= xe đạp nhanh hơn hoặc bằng xe hơi)
❌ The car is not as fast as the bike. (khi muốn nói "xe hơi nhanh hơn xe đạp") → ✅ The car is faster than the bike.

usage_notes.text: Với tính từ dài (hai âm tiết trở lên) không thêm -er/-est mà dùng more/less.
examples: ❌ The movie is interestinger → ✅ The movie is more interesting

usage_notes.text: Trong câu so sánh, tính từ luôn đứng sau chủ ngữ và trước 'than', không đảo vị trí.
examples: ❌ More crowded are the cities than rural areas → ✅ Cities are more crowded than rural areas
